business_context: MidTier Cloud, a 200-person B2B SaaS company selling project-management software, saw total revenue flat at $42M despite unit sales (seat licenses) growing 14% year-over-year. The CFO is confused why growth in customers isn't showing up in revenue.
correct_root_cause: Price erosion — the sales team has been discounting more heavily to win competitive deals; average realized price per seat has fallen 13% YoY while list price is unchanged.
optimal_data_pull_sequence: Revenue trend by month (confirm flat despite volume growth)
Unit volume trend (seats sold) by month
Average realized price per seat vs. list price, by quarter
Discount rate / win-rate on discounted deals by sales rep or region
why_distractor_is_tempting: Flat revenue alongside a crowded competitive market makes candidates jump to 'we're losing customers to competitors' before checking that volume is actually growing.

business_context: Harborline Freight, a regional trucking company with $180M in revenue, has seen operating margin compress from 11% to 6% over two quarters even though shipment volumes and per-shipment rates have both held steady.
correct_root_cause: Cost inflation — diesel fuel costs rose 22% and driver wages rose 9% due to a regional labor shortage, both flowing straight to COGS without a matching rate increase.
optimal_data_pull_sequence: Revenue and shipment volume trend (confirm both stable)
Realized rate per shipment/mile (confirm pricing unchanged)
COGS breakdown by line item (fuel, labor, maintenance) over the period
Fuel price index and regional wage data for the same period
incorrect_distractor_cause: Mix shift toward lower-margin shipment types
why_distractor_is_tempting: Margin compression with stable revenue naturally suggests the mix of business shifted toward cheaper, lower-margin routes rather than costs simply rising.

business_context: Solstice Apparel, a mid-market DTC clothing brand, has watched gross margin fall from 58% to 49% over the past three quarters. Marketing spend and customer traffic are both up, and unit sales volume is at an all-time high.
correct_root_cause: Price erosion — the brand leaned heavily on promotional codes and site-wide sales events to drive the traffic/volume growth, cutting average selling price per unit by 18%.
optimal_data_pull_sequence: Gross margin and revenue trend by quarter
Unit sales volume trend (confirm it's up, ruling out share loss)
Average selling price (net of discounts) vs. list price by quarter
Percent of orders using a promo code / average discount depth
incorrect_distractor_cause: Cost inflation in materials or shipping
why_distractor_is_tempting: A retail brand with falling margins immediately triggers thoughts of rising input or freight costs, especially given known apparel-industry cost headlines.

business_context: Beacon Dental Group, a 15-location dental services organization, has seen same-location patient visit volume drop 20% over the past two quarters while pricing per procedure and payer mix have remained unchanged.
correct_root_cause: Share loss — a new low-cost dental chain opened three locations within a mile of Beacon's busiest offices and is capturing new-patient volume, particularly among price-sensitive walk-ins.
optimal_data_pull_sequence: Patient visit volume trend by location, same-location basis
Price/reimbursement per procedure trend (confirm unchanged)
Payer/procedure mix trend (confirm unchanged)
New-patient acquisition trend and competitive openings near affected locations
why_distractor_is_tempting: Falling visit volume in a healthcare setting often gets misread as patients simply needing fewer visits (a mix/utilization story) rather than patients going elsewhere entirely.

business_context: Nimbus Mobile, a regional wireless carrier with 1.2M subscribers, reported flat ARPU but a net subscriber loss of 60,000 in the last two quarters after years of steady growth, even as churn-driving price and plan structure stayed the same.
correct_root_cause: Share loss — a national carrier launched an aggressive 5G bundle promotion in Nimbus's core metro markets, pulling subscribers away primarily at contract renewal.
optimal_data_pull_sequence: Subscriber count trend (gross adds vs. churn) by quarter
ARPU and plan pricing trend (confirm unchanged)
Churn reason codes / exit survey data
Competitor promotional activity and net subscriber trends in overlapping markets
incorrect_distractor_cause: Price erosion from aggressive retention discounting
why_distractor_is_tempting: Subscriber losses in telecom are so often tied to price wars that candidates assume Nimbus itself must have cut prices to compete, without checking that ARPU is actually flat.

business_context: Prairie Foods, a packaged snacks manufacturer selling to grocery chains, has seen total case volume shipped hold flat but net revenue per case fall 9% over the last three quarters, even though list prices to retailers have not changed.
correct_root_cause: Mix shift — retailers have shifted their ordering toward Prairie's smaller, lower-priced 'value pack' SKUs and away from the larger family-size SKUs, pulling down blended revenue per case despite unchanged unit pricing.
optimal_data_pull_sequence: Total case volume trend (confirm flat)
List price by SKU trend (confirm unchanged)
Revenue per case blended vs. by SKU/size tier
SKU mix (% of volume by pack size) trend over the same period
incorrect_distractor_cause: Price erosion via trade promotion spend
why_distractor_is_tempting: Falling net revenue per case looks like classic trade-discounting behavior in CPG, so candidates default to a pricing/promotion story instead of checking SKU mix.

business_context: Ironclad Fasteners, a B2B industrial parts distributor, has seen gross margin fall from 34% to 27% over four quarters. Sales volume in units is up 5%, and management insists supplier costs have been stable per their contracts.
correct_root_cause: Mix shift — large industrial accounts (which buy at deep volume-tier pricing and lower margin) have grown from 30% to 55% of unit volume, crowding out the higher-margin small-account/retail channel.
optimal_data_pull_sequence: Gross margin and revenue trend by quarter
Unit volume trend (confirm growth, ruling out share loss)
Supplier/input cost trend per unit (confirm stable, ruling out cost inflation)
Revenue and margin split by customer segment/channel (large accounts vs. small accounts) over time
why_distractor_is_tempting: Falling margins in a distribution business with rising input-cost headlines industry-wide makes 'our suppliers raised prices' the reflexive first guess.

business_context: Coastal Brew Co., a regional craft beverage company, has seen blended gross margin drop from 45% to 36% over two quarters. Total revenue is up 8% and total volume (cases) is up 11%, so leadership assumed things were going well until margin was flagged.
correct_root_cause: Mix shift — growth has come almost entirely from the lower-margin private-label/co-pack business for grocery chains, while the higher-margin branded product line has been flat, diluting blended margin even as top-line grows.
optimal_data_pull_sequence: Revenue and volume trend (confirm both growing)
Gross margin trend blended vs. by product line (branded vs. private-label)
Volume and revenue mix by product line over the same period
Per-unit pricing and cost by product line (confirm each line's own margin is stable)
incorrect_distractor_cause: Cost inflation in raw materials (hops, aluminum cans)
why_distractor_is_tempting: Beverage/CPG margin compression is widely associated with commodity input cost spikes, so that's the first hypothesis candidates reach for instead of checking the revenue mix.

business_context: Redwood HVAC Services, a residential HVAC installation and repair company operating in three metro markets, has seen operating margin fall from 22% to 14% over three quarters. Job volume and average job price are both flat.
correct_root_cause: Cost inflation — technician labor costs rose 15% due to a regional shortage of licensed HVAC techs forcing wage increases, and refrigerant costs rose sharply due to a regulatory phase-out of an older refrigerant type, both hitting job-level costs directly.
optimal_data_pull_sequence: Operating margin and revenue trend by quarter
Job volume and average job price trend (confirm both flat)
Cost per job breakdown (labor, materials/refrigerant, overhead) over time
Regional technician wage trend and refrigerant price trend over the same period
why_distractor_is_tempting: Margin decline in a competitive local services market is often blamed on losing better jobs to rivals, but job volume and pricing being flat should rule that out quickly.

business_context: Vantage Steel, a mid-size structural steel fabricator, has seen operating margin collapse from 18% to 9% in two quarters. Order backlog and shipped tonnage are both at record highs, and contract prices per ton were locked in before the drop began.
correct_root_cause: Cost inflation — steel coil (raw material input) prices spiked 30% due to a supply disruption, and because Vantage's contracts were fixed-price without cost-escalation clauses, the higher input cost was absorbed entirely as margin compression.
optimal_data_pull_sequence: Operating margin and shipped tonnage/revenue trend (confirm volume is not the issue)
Contract/realized price per ton trend (confirm fixed, ruling out price erosion)
Cost per ton breakdown, isolating raw material (steel coil) input cost
Steel coil market price index over the same period, and check contract escalation clause terms
incorrect_distractor_cause: Mix shift toward lower-margin project types
why_distractor_is_tempting: A fabricator with record volume but shrinking margin looks like it could be winning more of the 'wrong' (thinner-margin) projects, which distracts from checking the raw input cost line directly.

business_context: Aspen Outdoor Retail, a 40-store outdoor gear chain, has seen same-store revenue decline 12% over two quarters. Foot traffic per store is down 15%, while average transaction value and units per transaction have stayed roughly constant.
correct_root_cause: Share loss — a national e-commerce competitor expanded free same-day delivery into Aspen's core metro markets, pulling walk-in traffic toward online purchasing for the exact product categories Aspen specializes in.
optimal_data_pull_sequence: Same-store revenue trend by quarter
Foot traffic trend by store (confirm the decline is traffic-driven, not basket-driven)
Average transaction value and units per transaction trend (confirm unchanged)
Category-level online sales growth for competitors in overlapping trade areas
why_distractor_is_tempting: Declining store revenue in retail is commonly pattern-matched to markdown-driven price erosion, especially with outdoor gear's seasonal clearance cycles, before checking that transaction value is actually stable.

business_context: Lumen Analytics, a 60-person data analytics consultancy, has seen quarterly revenue fall from $9.5M to $7.8M even as the number of active client contracts held steady and average contract value was unchanged at signing.
correct_root_cause: Share loss — two of Lumen's five largest clients shifted a portion of their analytics work in-house after building internal data science teams, effectively reducing scope-of-work (and thus billed hours) on renewal — functionally the same loss-of-wallet-share dynamic as losing accounts to a rival.
optimal_data_pull_sequence: Revenue trend by quarter
Active contract count trend (confirm steady, ruling out simple attrition)
Contract value at signing vs. actual billed value at renewal, by top accounts
Client-level scope-of-work / hours billed trend for top 5 accounts, with renewal notes
why_distractor_is_tempting: Falling revenue with a stable client count and stable headline contract value looks like renewal-time discounting, when the real driver is shrinking scope/wallet share, not rate.
